blocks.text: Maple Ridge Acreages: the housing stock

items.t: Maple Ridge Zoning Bylaw No. 7600-2019 has agricultural zones A-1 through A-5: the City's own Shipping Container Guide (revised August 14, 2026) lists agricultural zones A-1 thru A-5 and names RS-1, RS-2 and RS-3 as rural residential zones that can also permit agriculture.

The City's compliance checklist covers only A1, A2 and A3 for one-family residential use, and records for each property whether it is in the ALR, in a flood plain, its minimum basement elevation and any geotechnical flag.

blocks.text: Maple Ridge Acreages: rules that affect buyers

items.t: ALR rules: subdivision needs Agricultural Land Commission (ALC) approval, an ALR residence cannot be stratified, a principal residence built without an ALC application is capped at 500 square metres (m²) with no more than 1,000 m² of fill, a suite is allowed only inside it, and one additional residence is capped at 90 m² (40 ha or less) or 186 m² (over 40 ha), with City bylaws also required to permit it.

Floodplain Management Bylaw No. 8121-2026 now designates floodplain across the city, including any land less than 1.5 m above the natural boundary of an adjacent watercourse, lake, pond, swamp, marsh or reservoir, and land inside the bylaw's floodplain setbacks.

Tree clearing for farming is under the Tree Protection and Management Bylaw No. 8045-2026: removing fewer than ten protected trees needs no permit where the land is in active agricultural use with active farm status, and that exemption does not apply to construction.

blocks.text: Maple Ridge Acreages: local details a buyer would not know

items.t: The City's A1 to A3 checklist sets agricultural buildings back 30 m from the front lot line and 15 m from rear and side lines, and mushroom buildings 60 m from the front line, distances an urban buyer does not expect.
The same checklist caps all agricultural buildings and structures at 20% lot coverage and greenhouse structures at 50%, with agricultural building height at 15 m.

A shipping container is allowed on an A-1 to A-5 lot only as an accessory to an agricultural use, and on an RS-1, RS-2 or RS-3 lot only where the lot is classified Farm under the Assessment Act and the container supports a farm operation.
Clearing more than 500 m² over a vulnerable aquifer while removing ten or more protected trees triggers a Groundwater Impact Assessment in the farm tree plan.

Farm class is income-tested in three tiers ($10,000 under 0.8 ha; $2,500 at 0.8 to 4 ha; $2,500 plus 5% of value over 4 ha), with applications by October 31, so a small bench acreage carries the strictest per-hectare test.

blocks.text: Maple Ridge Acreages: development and new projects

items.t: Status: adopted, implementation rolling out (as of November 3, 2026).

Hazards Framework, City of Maple Ridge: Council directed staff on March 11, 2026 to build a phased framework updating floodplain, geohazard, wildfire and ecosystem rules, with 2026 work focused on floodplain management and a city-wide hazard overview. Status: directed, in progress (as of November 3, 2026).

10225 272 Street, Whonnock side: a rezoning to allow a Farm Based Restaurant use on the subject property was adopted, per the City's July 28, 2026 Council Highlights. Status: adopted (as of November 3, 2026).

blocks.text: Maple Ridge Acreages: costs and taxes

items.t: Maple Ridge's 2026 total residential rate is 4.53578 per $1,000 of taxable value on the City's 2026 Property Tax Rate Summary, including a municipal general rate of 2.86430; taxes were due July 2, 2026.
The City adopted its 2026 to 2030 Financial Plan on May 12, 2026 with a 3.5% property tax increase, and flat-rate water and sewer for customers on that system are billed on the tax notice.

TransLink's system map lists Haney Place as the Maple Ridge hub, with the R3 Lougheed Highway RapidBus, route 701 to Coquitlam Central Station and Mission, route 748 to Thornhill, route 749 to Ruskin and route 595 from Maple Meadows Station across the Golden Ears Bridge to Langley Centre.
Maple Meadows and Port Haney are the city's West Coast Express stations on that map, which is the rail link acreage commuters use toward downtown Vancouver.

blocks.text: Maple Ridge Acreages: risks and due diligence

items.t: Look the parcel up first in Bylaw No. 8121-2026 Schedule A and its setback rules: the bylaw designates floodplain by hazard area and by the 1.5 m natural-boundary test, and its map does not state a parcel's ALR status or farm-class record.

Check ALR status separately on the ALC maps by parcel identifier (PID) or civic address; official confirmation comes from the ALC Mapping team, and the ALC map does not state a flood construction level.
On bench and upland parcels, add slope and watercourse checks: the City's Hazards Framework names slope instability and wildfire alongside flooding for Maple Ridge's upland and forested ground.
